column1: # jobleft occupation families: job-title phrases grouped into kinds of work, with how close two kinds are.
# Source: written new for jobleft by the match lane (2026-09-25). First-party data; no third-party list was copied.
# Licence: same as the jobleft project. Titles are common English job names.
# Format: family | label | implied industry (or -) | title phrases (comma list) | related families (family:weight)
#   * A title belongs to the family whose phrase covers the most words of the title; ties go to the phrase that
#     ends last (the head noun: "Nurse Recruiter" is a recruiter).
#   * A phrase that ends in $ must be the last words of the title or of one of its parts ("Server" is a job;
#     "Server Engineer" is not a server). Parts are split at " - ", ",", "|" and "(".
#   * "implied industry" is used only when a posting or a role says nothing else about its industry, and only for
#     kinds of work that almost always sit in one industry (a registered nurse works in healthcare).
#   * related weight: 1 = the same kind of work, 0.1 = unrelated. Missing pairs are unrelated. Pairs are symmetric.
